solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Angry Sri Lankan POW’s cynical notion of work (10,3)

indicatorNotes.Angry: letters in an angry state are stirred up and out of order

annotation.surface: A furious prisoner of war from Sri Lanka airs a jaundiced view of labour.
annotation.walkthrough: Parkinson's Law is the satirical maxim that work expands to fill the time available for its completion, hence 'cynical'.
annotation.definitionFit: Parkinson's Law is a wry, cynical observation about how work behaves.

entries.clue: Pal refusing to swim in Asian sea (7,4)

indicatorNotes.to swim: the letters swim about into a new order

annotation.surface: A friend on a beach holiday won't go into the water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To swim' reads as the thing the pal refuses; it is really the instruction to rearrange the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: The Persian Gulf is an arm of the sea in western Asia.

entries.clue: Mad boozer keels over unconscious (5)

indicatorNotes.keels over: something that keels over ends up upside down, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar
the id is the unconscious part of the mind in Freudian psychology

annotation.surface: A drunk in a pub collapses and passes out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like the drinker who keels over, but it is the pub itself; 'unconscious' is a noun here, Freud's id.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabid means mad, as in furious or fanatical.

entries.clue: Clean it up, shifting blame (9)

annotation.surface: Someone told to tidy up passes the buck to someone else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shifting blame' is a natural phrase, but 'shifting' belongs to the anagram and 'blame' stands alone as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the legal register: to accuse or incriminate, the opposite of exculpate.

entries.clue: Deliverer of bouquet nicking half of it (7)

indicatorNotes.nicking: the outer word nicks, or steals, the letter and holds it
indicatorNotes.half of: only half of the two-letter word is used

blocks.note: a wine's bouquet is its savour

annotation.surface: A florist delivering flowers pinches half of them along the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers to deliver, but it is a wine's aroma; 'nicking' is apt, since the deliverer steals from what is carried.
annotation.definitionFit: A saviour delivers people from danger or sin.

entries.clue: Emperor in tears, intermittently missing Old Dominion (5)

indicatorNotes.intermittently: only every other letter is taken
indicatorNotes.missing: the emperor with VA missing is what the alternate letters spell

blocks.note: the Old Dominion is a nickname of Virginia, abbreviated VA

annotation.surface: A weeping emperor, his tears now and then missing his old realm.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the emperor 'missing Old Dominion' leaves NER, so the solver adds VA back. Nerva was a Roman emperor (AD 96–98).
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: he ruled Rome AD 96–98 and adopted Trajan as his heir.

entries.clue: People watching lovely boy (7-2)

blocks.note: a lovely, a good-looking person, is a looker

annotation.surface: Onlookers admire a handsome young man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lovely' is a noun here, as in a beauty, not an adjective describing the boy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: onlookers, spectators at a scene.

entries.clue: Briefly crave pasty (3)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: cut short: the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A sudden short craving for a Cornish pasty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' reads as the pie you crave; it is the adjective meaning pale.
annotation.definitionFit: Pasty and wan both mean pale and unhealthy-looking.

entries.clue: Doughty at heart, fondle ferret (4)

indicatorNotes.at heart: the heart of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: to fondle is to stroke or rub

annotation.surface: A brave person cuddling a pet ferret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ferret' is a verb here, to rummage about, not the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: To grub about is to ferret, searching by digging or rummaging.

entries.clue: Report on particular fielder (5,5)

blocks.note: journalists cover, or report on, a story
a particular is a detail or point

annotation.surface: A journalist writes up one specific fielder.
annotation.walkthrough: Cover point is a fielding position in cricket, on the off side between point and cover; the name also serves for the player there.
annotation.definitionFit: Cover point is a cricket fielder stationed on the off side.

entries.clue: Complex flavonoid initially lacking in curry (8)

indicatorNotes.Complex: the letters are tangled into a complex arrangement
indicatorNotes.initially lacking: the word goes without its initial letter

blocks.note: FLAVONOID without its first letter F

annotation.surface: A chemist notes a curry is missing a particular plant compound.
annotation.walkthrough: A flavonoid is a plant pigment; 'complex' sounds like chemistry, but it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a fiery Goan dish, one kind of the general category.

entries.clue: Glimpse one impersonating copper (6)

blocks.note: one who apes, or mimics, is an aper
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A fleeting sight of someone pretending to be a police officer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer to go with the impersonator; it is the element.
annotation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief glimpse or insight.

entries.clue: Tragedy of feline pet throttled by alpha male (11)

indicatorNotes.throttled by: the pet is gripped round the neck, held inside the other letters

blocks.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, a strop

annotation.surface: A cat dies after a dominant man strangles it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alpha male' reads as a single idea but splits in two around the pet, which here means a sulk, not an animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a calamity or disaster, the sense of a dreadful event rather than the stage genre.

entries.clue: Writer’s gripped by odd sound (10)

indicatorNotes.gripped by: the writer's letters are held inside the other word

blocks.note: the writer of the clue says 'I am', I'M

annotation.surface: An author is struck by a strange noise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is the setter's I'M, not a possessive; 'sound' is the adjective meaning intact, not a noise.
annotation.definitionFit: Something sound is unimpaired, whole and undamaged.

entries.clue: Death of ethics over time (9)

indicatorNotes.over: the word lies over, covering, the letter

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: Moral codes wither away as the years go by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' here means covering, so the ethics word wraps round the time letter rather than coming after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: loss of life, counted in number as in infant rates, or simply being subject to dying.

entries.clue: Dry and extremely delicate late husband cocked up on drug (9)

indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, first and last letters, are used
indicatorNotes.cocked up: turned upward, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: the first and last letters of DELICATE
h is the abbreviation for husband
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

annotation.surface: A dainty widow is described as dry and messed up on drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late husband' reads as a dead spouse; the two words are separate pieces that go up the grid together, above the drug.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to remove the water from something.

entries.clue: Smart set regularly wasted stuff (4)

indicatorNotes.regularly wasted: every other letter is thrown away

blocks.note: the odd letters of SmArT sEt

annotation.surface: The fashionable crowd get drunk on stuff at every party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like drunk, the smart set's state; here it discards letters. 'Stuff' is a verb: stuff oneself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to fill someone up until they can take no more.

entries.clue: Express contentment, parking posh luxury car (4)

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

annotation.surface: A driver feels smug after parking a smart luxury car.
annotation.walkthrough: The purr is also what a fine engine does, which is why the car fits the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: The low vibrating sound a pleased cat makes, extended to a person's satisfied murmur.

entries.clue: Ribaldry and ebullience when Henry moves (10)

indicatorNotes.moves: one letter moves to a new place in the word

blocks.note: H, the henry (unit of inductance), is the letter that moves, from the front to after EART

annotation.surface: A king named Henry gets bawdy and exuberant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a king; it is the H, symbol for the henry, which moves inside HEARTINESS.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthiness is coarse, ribald frankness.

entries.clue: Mostly depended on village’s banks for aid (7)

indicatorNotes.Mostly: most of the word, all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.banks: a word's banks are its edges, first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of VILLAGE

annotation.surface: A village leaned on the riverbanks for help.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests a river or money; it means the outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to help or bring assistance, as in lifting a siege.

entries.clue: Look after a fine female pigeon (6)

indicatorNotes.after: this piece comes after the others

blocks.note: a look or appearance is an air

annotation.surface: Someone asks another to care for a handsome hen pigeon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as a phrase meaning tend; it splits into Look and after. 'Not my pigeon' is a British idiom for 'not my affair'.
annotation.definitionFit: Your pigeon, in the idiom, is your concern or affair.

entries.clue: Port and fine German wine (5)

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port

annotation.surface: A wine list offering port and a good German white.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' reads as another wine; it is a harbour city, Rio.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a red from northern Spain, one kind of the general category.

entries.clue: Swift perhaps to pursue boy with unknown bug (8)

indicatorNotes.to pursue: the bird follows, coming after the rest

blocks.note: a swift is a kind of bird

annotation.surface: A fast creature chases a boy and an unidentified insect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swift' reads as an adjective or Jonathan Swift; it is the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A ladybird is a small beetle, a bug in the loose sense; Americans call it a ladybug.

entries.clue: Try and empty elegant basin (5)

indicatorNotes.empty: the word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: a try, an attempt, is a bid

annotation.surface: An invitation to try out a stylish bathroom fitting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Empty' is a common way to ask for just the outer letters of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a low bathroom bowl for washing, one kind of the general category.

entries.clue: Patience maybe of one manager overwhelmed by stupor (5,5)

indicatorNotes.overwhelmed by: the letters are engulfed by the surrounding word

blocks.note: one who copes, or manages, is a coper

annotation.surface: A dazed manager has lost all his patience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Patience' reads as the virtue or the card game; it is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, hence 'maybe'.
annotation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience is an example of a comic opera.

entries.clue: Random piece of period drama (3)

indicatorNotes.piece of: the answer is a piece cut from the words that follow

annotation.surface: An arbitrary snippet from a costume drama.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the two words, which is typical of a hidden word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: occasional or haphazard, as in the odd job.

entries.clue: Low-down half-wit (4)

blocks.note: a noun here: inside information, the facts

annotation.surface: A mean, contemptible idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low-down' looks like an adjective describing the half-wit; it is the noun, and dope is slang for both the facts and the fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Dope means both inside information and a stupid person.

entries.clue: Re-enacted racy plays in support facility (3-4,6)

indicatorNotes.plays: the letters are played about with

annotation.surface: Saucy dramas are restaged at a care home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racy plays' looks like the thing re-enacted; 'plays' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A place giving daytime care to children or the elderly, described by its function.
